newsitem.title: KENYA: Sudanese rebels say they seized back town.
newsitem.headline: Sudanese rebels say they seized back town.

text.p: Sudanese rebels said on Wednesday they had recaptured the town of Chali el-Fil near the border with Ethiopia from government forces which seized it at the weekend.

Sampson Kwaje, spokesman for the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), said SPLA forces on Monday attacked and recaptured the southeastern town, shot down a helicopter gunship and seized arms and ammunition. He said the three-man helicopter crew died.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.
Sudanese President Lieutenant-General Omar Hassan al-Bashir announced the government's seizure of Chali el-Fil on Sunday from the SPLA, which had captured it in a rebel offensive in January.
Khartoum said Ethiopian and Eritrean troops did most of the fighting for the rebels. Both countries and Uganda have denied fighting alongside the rebels.

The rebel say they are going to seize the southern capital of Juba, which is heavily defended, following the capture of the major southern town of Yei last Wednesday and the fall on Saturday of a garrison 100 km (60 miles) south of the city.

The SPLA has been fighting since 1983 for greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem Arabised north but has made significant gains since the start of its offensive in January.
